---
title: "Plan Sealing and Canonical Identity"
subtitle: "When is a Plan immutable, and what is safe to share?"
toc-depth: 2
---

**Status:** `CONVERGING` implementation design.

## Seal once at the Run boundary

`CircuitPlan` remains editable only during authoring. `CircuitRun(plan=...,
workspace=...)` validates and permanently seals a canonical snapshot. The Run
then supports any number of Refs, Specs, and ParameterSets against that
snapshot. Execution never mutates it.

A change to sealed topology, an authoring baseline, Ports, couplings, or a
public component schema creates a new Plan, Run, and workspace binding. A
parameter value selected through a declared `ParameterRef` and supplied in a
`ParameterSet` does not. Multiple sealed Runs may coexist in one kernel; no
global epoch invalidates an older Run.

## Separate three identities

| Identity | Includes | Excludes |
|---|---|---|
| Plan | canonical component schemas, topology, nodes, ground, Ports, couplings, baselines, and catalog source identity | workspace path, display theme, execution history |
| Request | Plan, Ref lineage, Spec, bound ParameterSet, operation, and numerical runtime | workspace location, progress display, and attempt history |
| Evidence | request plus workspace binding, source units, runtime files, attempt, artifacts, and receipt hashes | mutable latest pointers |

Physical values cross the computation boundary as coherent-SI magnitude,
canonical SI unit, and declared dimensionality. Source unit and authoring form
remain evidence. Consequently `92 * u.fF` and `0.092 * u.pF` may share semantic
computation identity while retaining distinct provenance.

## Canonicalize before hashing

Python emits UTF-8 canonical JSON with deterministic object-key order and
explicit type/schema tags. It rejects NaN, infinity, pickle payloads, and
absolute machine paths. Arrays are referenced by relative artifact identity
rather than embedded as enormous JSON lists.

Catalog provenance binds the public catalog class/module and exact obtainable
distribution or source identity. If a component instance cannot prove that
identity at seal time, sealing fails; a display name is not sufficient.

The Plan snapshot, request JSON, and receipt each carry their own schema and
hash. Hashing the containing workspace directory is not an identity protocol.
